What we do

Clean pours,
proper finish

Concrete flatwork looks simple — until it fails. Cracking, spalling, settling, and drainage problems almost always trace back to the same root causes: poor sub-base preparation, wrong mix design, inadequate reinforcement, or improper curing.

We don't cut corners on any of it. Every pour starts with a properly prepared and compacted base. Every slab gets the right reinforcement for its load. Every finish is done right — not rushed before the pour goes off.

  • Sub-base grading, compaction, and preparation
  • Steel reinforcement where required by spec or load
  • Proper mix design for the application and climate
  • Control joints cut to spec to manage cracking
  • Correct drainage slope built into every pour
  • ADA compliance handled on every applicable surface
  • Permits pulled and managed by our team
Who we work with
Property managers, building owners, general contractors, municipalities, and institutions across the Tri-State area. Commercial and municipal concrete is our specialty — we understand the compliance requirements, the scheduling constraints, and what it takes to keep a busy property operational during a pour.
Typical project size
From single sidewalk panels and ADA ramp replacements to full parking lot concrete replacements spanning thousands of square feet. We scope and staff every job correctly regardless of size.
Scheduling around your property
Concrete pours require access and cure time. We plan the work sequence around your property's operational needs — staging areas, access routes, and phasing are all accounted for before we show up.
What you get
A straight quote, a real crew, and a clean site when we leave. No change orders, no surprises.
Scope of work

Everything we cover

Sidewalks & walkways

Full lot replacement
Complete demolition of failed concrete, sub-base rework, reinforcement, and full pour — for lots that are past the point of repair.
06
Repairs & saw-cutting
Targeted concrete repairs for cracked panels, settled sections, and utility cuts — saw-cut edges, proper bonding, matched finish.
The craft behind it

What separates
good concrete

Most concrete looks the same the day it's poured. The difference shows up over years — in whether it cracks, whether it settles, whether it holds its grade and drains properly.

  • i.Base preparation — we don't pour over bad ground. Sub-base is graded, compacted, and inspected before forms go in.
  • ii.Right reinforcement — rebar or wire mesh sized to the load and slab thickness. Not an afterthought.
  • iii.Proper jointing — control joints placed and cut at the right spacing to manage where cracking occurs.
  • iv.Finish and cure — broom finish, edge work, and adequate curing time. We don't rush the last steps.
Our process

How every concrete
project runs

Step one
Site assessment
We walk the site to evaluate existing conditions, sub-base, drainage, access, and scope of work needed.
Step two
Proposal
Clear, itemized quote covering demo, base work, reinforcement, pour, and finish. No vague line items.
Step three
Demo & prep
Existing concrete removed, sub-base graded and compacted. Forms set and inspected before any concrete is ordered.
Step four
Pour & finish
Concrete placed, screeded, floated, and finished. Control joints cut. Crew on site until the pour is done right.
Step five
Cure & handoff
Adequate cure time before the surface is opened to traffic. Site cleaned and handed back to you in full working order.
